=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5637 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The judge context filter only excludes `<!-- ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` comments, so V2 state chunks pass through into `recent_comments`.
  WHY: The same base64 state noise that was filtered out for V1 can now waste judge context and revive the argv-length failure this filter was meant to prevent.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7828 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The warning still says no valid `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` comment was found even though V2 extraction was tried first.
  WHY: That message can send operators looking for a missing V1 comment instead of diagnosing a broken V2 reassembly path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8251, 8299 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `/revalidate` and `/judge_resume` only search for `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1`, so the latest V2 state comment is ignored when computing the last state index.
  WHY: `$last_state_idx` can point to an older V1 comment, letting already-processed commands be treated as new and re-executed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1069-1098 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `post_state_comment` can return success after posting zero V2 chunks because `.files[]` extraction can collapse to an empty loop.
  WHY: If the manifest/JQ path yields no chunk files, the function returns 0 and the tracking issue keeps stale state, so the poller continues on unpersisted V1 data.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1108 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The jq wrapper for chunk payloads suppresses stderr, so malformed or truncated chunk files fail with only the generic `jq failed to wrap chunk payload` message.
  WHY: Without the underlying jq error, packer or filesystem corruption is hard to diagnose after a torn state-write chain.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1144-1156 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The `gh api` failure annotation truncates stderr to 4 KiB, so larger GitHub API errors lose detail.
  WHY: Rate-limit or validation responses can repeat without enough context to explain why the chunk post failed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1170-1213 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The V2 extractor call discards stderr, so Python crashes or parse/runtime errors are indistinguishable from the intended no-chain fallback.
  WHY: Missing dependencies, corrupt inputs, or extractor bugs fall back to V1 with no diagnostic, hiding broken V2 persistence.
- scripts/orchestrate_state_v2.py:150-170 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: Invalid V2 chunk base64 is swallowed as a silent `None` result instead of being distinguished from an incomplete chain.
  WHY: Corrupted chunks force an unannounced fallback to stale V1 state.
- scripts/detect_editor_changes_lost.sh:62-93 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The sed rule only strips reference clauses at end-of-line, so mid-line references can survive extraction.
  WHY: A healthy commit can be flagged with `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` because referenced filenames leak into the edit set.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:575-763 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: A codex run that exits 0 after SIGTERM at the per-attempt timeout boundary can still proceed through validation with partially resolved tree state.
  WHY: The timeout handling does not explicitly distinguish this edge case, so validation context can reflect an incomplete merge resolution.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:661-677 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `CONFLICT_RESOLVER_PER_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS` accepts any positive integer without a minimum floor.
  WHY: Very small values can burn all retry attempts on immediate timeouts, aborting the resolver before meaningful work.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:116-198, 212-234 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: `_looks_like_re_escape_output` can misclassify escaped regex metacharacters and drop valid `must_not_contain` checks.
  WHY: A forbidden pattern containing regex syntax can slip past verification, letting regressions through silently.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3762-3866 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_probe_resolver` truncates `bash -n` stderr to a sanitized single line in the triple-failure path.
  WHY: Large parse errors lose the context needed to explain why the resolver entry point is unusable.

  WHY: `$last_state_idx` can resolve to an older V1 comment, so commands after the last V1 write can be treated as new and re-executed.

  PROBLEM: The V2 extractor invocation discards all stderr via `2>/dev/null`.
  WHY: Plumbing failures from `orchestrate_state_v2.py` are indistinguishable from the intended no-chain path, so the poller can silently fall back to stale V1.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1108 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_post_state_comment_v2_chunk` discards jq stderr when wrapping the chunk file into a JSON payload.
  WHY: A malformed, empty, or truncated chunk file yields only a generic jq failure message, which makes the root cause hard to diagnose.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1082 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The chunk-files extraction `jq -r '.files[]' 2>/dev/null || true` silently collapses a jq failure into an empty loop.
  WHY: If jq fails after the manifest validated, the function can post zero chunks and still return success, leaving the state unpersisted.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7828 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The warning text says "No valid ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1 comment found for tracking issue #..." even though V2 extraction was tried first and also failed.
